newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: SFE wheat holds up against Chicago slide.
newsitem.headline: SFE wheat holds up against Chicago slide.

text.p: Sydney Futures Exchange (SFE) wheat futures edged down on Friday but resisted the sharp downturn on Chicago overnight.
"In comparison to Chicago's fall last night, it (SFE wheat) provides very good selling for growers and merchants," one broker said.
January 1998, the only contract to trade, fell by A$1.00 to A$172.00 in five trades, while the contract's settlement price came back by 50 cents to A$172.50.
Settlement prices generally edged down by 50 cents to A$1.00, with more distant contracts falling least and the two nearest-term contracts down by A$1.50 and A$2.50 respectively.
This compared with Chicago's sharp downturn overnight when May wheat fell 13 1/2 cents to US$3.75 a bushel.
The Australian market was leaning toward downside over the next couple of days, the broker said.
"Whether it bounces back (remains to be) seen. There might be a day of consolidation, we'll see what happens after that," he said.
